title: CMTD: Cognitive Modeling with Traits and Distortions for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent; zero-shot setting stated in Sec. 4)

task.subset_rule: all (MELD test set: 2,610 utterances in 280 dialogues; one call per dialogue)
task.approximation: the printed Text-only prompt gives no label set or output format: the reply is parsed for one of the seven MELD labels per numbered utterance (synonyms mapped), unlabelled utterances count as wrong; conversation rendered as numbered 'Speaker: utterance' lines (rendering not printed)

items.source: https://github.com/declare-lab/MELD, file data/MELD/test_sent_emo.csv (also in the HF mirror zrr1999/MELD_Text)

fields_prose.input: Utterance, Speaker (grouped by Dialogue_ID, ordered by Utterance_ID)
fields_prose.label: Emotion (neutral, joy, surprise, anger, sadness, disgust, fear)

items.columns_verified: Sr No., Utterance, Speaker, Emotion, Sentiment, Dialogue_ID, Utterance_ID, Season, Episode, StartTime, EndTime (2,610 rows, 280 dialogues; Emotion counts neutral 1256, joy 402, anger 345, surprise 281, sadness 208, disgust 68, fear 50)

prompt.user_template:
Based on the provided conversation, identify the primary emotion expressed for each utterance in the conversation.
The conversation is as follows: {conversation}

placeholders_prose.conversation: all utterances of the dialogue as numbered 'Speaker: utterance' lines

output.parse: label from set [neutral, joy, surprise, anger, sadness, disgust, fear]
output.postprocess: lowercase; map synonyms (happy -> joy, sad -> sadness, angry -> anger, surprised -> surprise, disgusted -> disgust, scared/afraid -> fear); missing labels count as wrong
output.parse_prose: label from set [neutral, joy, surprise, anger, sadness, disgust, fear] per utterance: for each numbered utterance take the first label word on its line, else in order of appearance

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 2,610 test utterances whose predicted emotion equals the gold Emotion, in percent
metric.original_location: Table 2, MELD block, row gpt-4.1-nano, column Text-only ACC (weighted F1 39.34)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare 2026-09-07: est_usd_prepare counts <=400 output tokens per free-text call (runner out_guess); est_usd_dryrun_max_tokens counts the full max_tokens

open_points: [triage 2026-09-09 g1] Scoring of free-text emotion phrases is unreported by the paper: choose a mapping rule (offline, no API calls; strict 13.2% vs extended synonym map about 31% vs paper 42.45), or accept as a protocol gap. A prompt carrying the label set would be our design, not the paper's (840 calls x 3 seeds, about USD 0.02-0.36).
notes: The repository (Shaun-le/CMTD, prompts/text_only.txt) may carry an output-format line that the paper's Table 6 omits; the paper version is used. Calls are per dialogue (280 x 3 seeds); bootstrap over utterances as the paper's accuracy unit. Weighted F1 (39.34) is a free second check. || [hook 2026-09-07] load_items() groups the 2,610 MELD test utterances into 280 dialogues (numbered 'Speaker: utterance' lines, gold = list of Emotion labels); parse() reads one label per numbered line (synonyms mapped) or the labels in order of appearance; score() = per-utterance accuracy (bootstrap over utterances), weighted F1 printed. n_items = 2,610 utterances scored from 280 calls per seed. || [triage 2026-09-09 g1] MIXED / protocol gap. The printed Text-only prompt is identical to prompts/text_only.txt in Shaun-le/CMTD (checked 2026-09-09: no label set, no output format). gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 (pinned) answers with free emotion phrases per numbered utterance ('Curious or inquisitive', 'Encouragement / Support', 'Excitement / happiness', 'Neutral / informative'); the 7-label + small-synonym parse leaves 1,705 of 2,610 utterances unlabelled -> 13.2% (per seed 13.4/12.9/13.3; 27 of 280 replies fully unparsed per seed). Sensitivity with an extended deterministic synonym map (scratch script, not in the hook): 31.2/29.9/31.8%, 111 unlabelled. Paper 42.45. The paper does not state how free text was mapped to the MELD labels.
